parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for a complete installable Mootdx package with pyproject metadata, root exports, Reader and Quotes factories, Affair, server utilities, CLI commands, DataFrame conversion, and local tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent retained implementation and delivery ownership while delegating research-only work to three children for API reference, binary formats, and network clients.
parallel.implementation: The parent cloned the upstream Mootdx repository, then patched pyproject metadata, root package exports, reader and quotes module-level factories, config, exceptions, utilities, financial/tools exports, server selection, and API-surface tests.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent integrated its own patches in the shared workspace, cleaned temporary export artifacts, checked git status, installed the workspace in editable mode, and produced a final response describing intentional files.
parallel.verification: Parallel ran the original upstream tests before patching, then focused API checks, then the full local suite with 100 passed and 48 skipped, plus editable-install and import checks; it could not invoke submit inside the agent session.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation later failed 10 hidden tests despite local success, so remaining gaps were hidden-suite compatibility or behavioral coverage issues rather than a visible unjoined child result.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Mootdx API, packaging, CLI, reader, quote, financial, server, utility, caching, and test requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned the whole implementation path: inspect environment, extract the published package, patch compatibility gaps, add packaging and tests, then verify locally.
serial.implementation: The serial run extracted the published wheel into the empty workspace and patched root exports, config, exceptions, utilities, contrib/tools/financial exports, reader factories, CLI handling, custom sectors, affair behavior, server selection, quotes helpers, and packaging files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because there were no child outputs, all integration decisions stayed in one timeline; after initial failed broad patching it made smaller patches and installed the workspace package to replace a broken editable distribution.
serial.verification: Serial used compileall, import smoke checks, CLI help, pyproject inspection, and a local pytest suite that passed 7 tests; it also could not invoke submit inside the agent session.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation failed 12 hidden tests, leaving more hidden-suite gaps than the parallel run and reflecting a narrower local validation suite and different implementation choices.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the broad Mootdx requirements and used the upstream repository plus child research to cover public API and package metadata.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same broad requirements and used the published wheel as a baseline for a self-contained package.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No meaningful requirements-discovery difference is evidenced; both attempted the required API, but parallel added broader regression coverage and shipped a larger upstream-derived tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split research into API-reference, binary-format, and network-client children while the parent kept implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all work in one agent and tracked package creation, implementation, CLI, and verification in a single plan.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had research fan-out but no delegated implementation ownership; serial had no coordination boundary and no child dependency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child handoffs returned API, binary, and network findings, and the parent continued applying patches after receiving them.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial acquired the same context directly from installed metadata, wheel contents, source files, and dependency inspection.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff boundaries, but the record does not show a lost, stale, conflicting, or unusably bulky handoff that caused the hidden-test failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel cloned the upstream repository and patched a broad source tree, including metadata, exports, utility behavior, exceptions, server helpers, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial extracted the wheel and applied compatibility edits into that smaller artifact-derived workspace after one broad patch failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel preserved more upstream repository assets and tests; serial constructed a leaner package from the wheel and added fewer local regression tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited once too briefly, then later received all three child reports and continued parent-owned implementation and validation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; it proceeded through local implementation, local verification, package install, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The extra parallel result lifecycle did not produce a missing join or trapped result; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared the workspace with read-only research children while the parent made source changes and then checked git status and cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one writer and performed all integration in a single workspace, including replacing a broken installed editable package with the workspace copy.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared workspace visibility but no observed child writes, overwrite, or provenance confusion; serial had no concurrent shared-state risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran upstream tests, focused API checks, full local pytest with 100 passed and 48 skipped, editable install, and import tests, but could not run submit.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran compileall, local pytest with 7 passed, CLI and packaging smoke checks, editable install, and also could not run submit.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel local verification was broader and aligned with the larger upstream tree, yet both missed hidden evaluator cases; serial local tests were substantially narrower.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished within the agent budget, all children completed, and final closure stated the official submit tool was unavailable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also finished within the agent budget and closed after local tests, package install, and checking that submit was unavailable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no timeout-driven outcome difference; both closed due to unavailable in-session submit and later failed official evaluation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official completed evaluations show both attempts failed, with parallel at 82/92 and serial at 80/92. Parallel did somewhat better by cloning the full upstream repository and running a broader local suite, while serial built from the wheel and verified only a smaller local surface. This is a material implementation-coverage difference but not a discordant official pass/fail outcome and not a directly evidenced parallel coordination error.
parallel_contributors: The parent cloned the upstream repository and retained more project assets and upstream tests before patching.
The parent used child research reports as advisory context while still owning implementation and verification.
serial_contributors: The serial run extracted the wheel and patched a smaller workspace with fewer tests.
The serial run recovered from a failed broad patch and environment import issues but ended with only 7 local tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel shipped broader upstream-derived source and tests; serial shipped a leaner wheel-derived package.
Both relied on local validation because submit was not exposed inside the agent session.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative implementation coverage difference, not an outcome-discordant or concurrency-specific root cause
